newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank 100 and 200 mark notes get new security.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank 100 and 200 mark notes get new security.

text.p: Two German banknotes will soon have new security features to fend off counterfeiters and help with the transition to the single European currency, the Bundesbank said on Monday.

The basic appearance of the central bank's 100 and 200 mark notes, the denominations that counterfeiters try to copy the most, will not be changed as banknotes without the new features will remain in circulation.

Instead, the new notes will have special illustrated foils -- similar to those on some credit cards -- that show different motifs and colours when tilted, along with other features such as latent images, security thread and watermarks.
The first new 100 and 200 mark notes will be put into circulation beginning on August 1, and will then be followed by improved 50 mark notes at the start of next year.
About 70 percent of the current 1.1 billion 100 mark notes in circulation will be exchanged by next summer, the Bundesbank said.

The new bills will also be helpful when the mark is replaced by the euro to fend off counterfeit notes as 30 to 40 percent of German banknotes circulate outside the country, particularly in eastern Europe.
Counterfeiting is not a major problem for the Bundesbank, which said that it had found 25,800 cases of falsified banknotes worth about four million marks.
